about: The benchmark set (plans/map-quality-plan.md). Each brief is generic, so it works for any campaign. `want` is the character the map should have, as [min, max] ranges on profile features (map-plan/similar.mjs WANT_FEATURES; null = no bound; `enclosure` is the share of the map's area inside rooms); it grades a made map and queries the shelf. `play` is what the scene must do at the table. Every sprint's review re-makes these and scores them on the rubric. `words` are theme words matched against a published map's pack and scene names (catalogue metadata, never the art): the shelf narrows by words, then ranks by character. Briefs v2 (2026-11-03): theme (vocab.json tags), contents (kinds wanted) and describe (for the picture search) beside want; words stay for the name-only search. Briefs v3 (2026-11-04): two S0 guesses corrected after the first made maps and 1,381 published ones were measured. ruined-fort enclosure [0.3, 0.8] -> [0.05, 0.6]: a breached ruin's yard is open ground (published forts measure 0 to 0.2). sewer-junction enclosure [0.4, -] -> [0.2, -] and rooms [4, 10] -> [3, 10]: tunnels cut in rock leave most of the map rock (the published sewer layout measures 0.04 and 3 rooms). Published maps are walled lightly for Foundry (most have no loops and few doors), so their numbers describe the shelf, not a target for a made map.

rubric.look: Does it read as the place at a glance, from a token's eye, in the scene's light? Edges, light, a focal point, a frame that isn't flat fill.
rubric.play: Does the fight or the scene work? Cover where it's needed, a reason to move, more than one route, exits players can see. Graded by the play check, then by the GM.
rubric.fit: Can it drop into a scene with little work: walls, doors and lights right, size and shape close to what was asked, variants to hand.
rubric.speed: Minutes from asking to a walled, lit scene: under 2 from the shelf; under 30 for a made map, Dungeondraft render included.

briefs.title: Sewer junction
briefs.brief: Brick tunnels meet at a junction with a deeper channel through it. Walkways either side, a sluice gate, a side room for the workers.
briefs.play: A chase or an ambush from the water. Two ways out besides the way in; a choke at the sluice.
briefs.tests: Masonry and water. The regression check against our long gallery.
briefs.describe: brick sewer tunnels meeting at a junction, a water channel with walkways either side

briefs.title: Cave with a river and a ledge
briefs.brief: A cave mouth opens into a hall; an underground river runs through a second chamber below a ledge; a side passage loops back.
briefs.play: Height matters: a ledge to hold, a river to cross, a loop to flank by.
briefs.describe: a cave with an underground river and a rocky ledge above it

briefs.title: Desert wash ambush
briefs.brief: A dry riverbed winds between low cliffs. Boulders and scrub in the wash; a goat path up one side.
briefs.play: Ambushers on the cliffs, travellers in the wash. Long sightlines, with cover only where it was placed.
briefs.tests: Outdoor cliffs, long sightlines against cover.
briefs.describe: a dry desert riverbed winding between low cliffs, boulders and scrub

briefs.title: Crooked night market
briefs.brief: A crooked street opening onto a small square, lined with shopfronts and stalls under lanterns; an alley off it.
briefs.play: A social scene that can become a chase. Crowds to hide in, lots of ways out.
briefs.tests: Irregular lots and buildings, stalls, spots for background people.
briefs.describe: a crowded market street and small square lined with stalls and shopfronts

briefs.title: Temple hall
briefs.brief: A pillared hall on one axis, side chapels, a raised sanctum at the far end, a sacristy behind it.
briefs.play: A set piece: a long approach, pillars for cover, a stage at the end.
briefs.tests: Formal and symmetric: square done right.
briefs.describe: a pillared temple hall with an altar on a raised sanctum and side chapels

briefs.title: Ruined fort, overgrown
briefs.brief: A square fort with one tower fallen. A breach in the curtain wall, rubble in the yard, trees growing through the barracks.
briefs.play: A siege or a search. The breach is a second way in; rubble gives cover.
briefs.tests: Masonry plus wear, collapse and plants.
briefs.describe: a ruined stone fort with a breached wall, rubble and trees in the yard

briefs.title: Ship at a dock
briefs.brief: A two-masted ship tied up at a stone quay, a gangway down, crates and a crane on the quay, water all round.
briefs.play: A boarding or a fight on the quay. The gangway is the choke; the water is a hazard.
briefs.describe: a sailing ship moored at a stone quay with crates and a crane, water all round

briefs.title: Forest or swamp clearing
briefs.brief: A clearing in old woods with a stream at one edge, a fallen tree across it, thick trees round the outside.
briefs.play: An encounter on the road. Trees and roots as cover, the stream as a slow crossing.
briefs.describe: a clearing in old woods with a stream and a fallen tree

briefs.title: Tavern interior
briefs.brief: A common room with a bar and a hearth, a kitchen behind, a back room, stairs up, a door to the yard.
briefs.play: The everyday drop-in: a talk, a brawl, a quick exit through the kitchen.
briefs.tests: A small, square interior that must be fast to find on the shelf.
briefs.describe: a tavern common room with tables, a bar counter and a fireplace
